sentence: This project uses human vascularized cardiac organoids and multi-omics to study what causes cardiovascular problems in Down syndrome.
This project studies how neurotransmitter receptors that regulate central nervous system function are built, signal and interact with drugs.
This project works to advance a therapeutic for metastatic melanoma, a skin cancer with limited effective treatment options.
This project builds a camera-based system that checks medication at the moment of use to catch medication errors at the point of care.
This project builds an assay that profiles single cells in tissue sections to understand how cells organize and communicate.
This project studies how immune responses and beta cell killing are related in type 1 diabetes, to find ways to prevent beta cell loss.
This project studies how genetic background affects the biology and evolution of Cryptococcus neoformans, a common cause of fungal meningitis.
This project studies how rural context protects low-income children from drug use problems by looking at neural risk processes.
This project coordinates communication, data sharing and oversight among research teams working at the interface of immunology and gerontology.
This project tests a theranostic in multiple cancer models to learn what makes tumors sensitive to radiation.
This project studies how a form of autophagy, the cells' waste and recycling system, contributes to blood cancer formation and therapy resistance.
This project builds a blood test that uses CRISPR to detect Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA in patients.
This project studies how brain networks decline in aging, epilepsy and neurodegenerative diseases and how this differs from healthy aging.
This project studies how genetic variants cause Alzheimer's disease by looking at their effects in different brain cell types and ancestral populations.
This project studies how the mammary gland and metabolic tissue communicate through mammokines in health and disease, using mouse models of metabolic disorders.
This project studies how microglia cause inflammation and neuron loss in glaucoma.
This project studies how a carbohydrate binding protein stops coronavirus infection and whether it also works on variants and related coronaviruses.
This project studies how repeated morphine exposure changes somatostatin interneurons in the prelimbic cortex and how this affects opioid seeking behavior.
This project studies how Herpes Simplex Virus copies its DNA, to understand the basic mechanisms of viral DNA replication.
This project builds computer models of the tumor-immune microenvironment to help design sequences of immunotherapy and targeted inhibitor treatments for melanoma.
